narrative:
The model determined that you have a 39% chance of being a bad credit risk. Because this probability is high enough to cross the bank's approval threshold, your loan application was denied.

The three factors that most strongly influenced this outcome were the status of your checking account, the length of the loan you requested, and the total amount you wanted to borrow. Your checking account status was the most important reason for the denial. Having a negative balance pushes the prediction noticeably toward bad credit risk, especially since most approved applicants (about 59%) have no checking account at all or maintain positive balances.

The duration of the loan worked in your favor. At 15 months, your request was shorter than the 19-month average among approved loans, which helped reduce your risk score. Similarly, the loan amount of 1,721 DM was well below the 3,020 DM average seen in approved applications, giving another moderate push toward approval.

Unfortunately, the negative effect from your checking account status outweighed these positive signals. 

To improve your chances next time, bring your checking account balance back into positive territory before reapplying. This single change would likely have the biggest impact on lowering your risk score. Consider starting with a smaller, shorter loan once your account is healthier, then build a stronger credit history over time.
